_note: Species morphology pool (§8). `sensorReading` is the pre-contact sensor blurb used by the first-contact flow — what your instruments see before you can talk to them.

morphologies.name: Avian
morphologies.sensorReading: Hollow-boned lifesigns, high metabolic burn. Their ships ride thermals that do not exist — flocking patterns in hard vacuum.

morphologies.name: Fungal Collective
morphologies.sensorReading: One lifesign, or ten thousand — the sensors cannot decide. Spore density in the hull atmosphere is off every chart you have.

morphologies.name: Machine
morphologies.sensorReading: No biology at all. Clock-regular power signatures, and a comms band that sounds like arithmetic arguing with itself.

morphologies.name: Gaseous
morphologies.sensorReading: Pressure vessels where crew quarters should be. The lifesigns diffuse and reform — beings of weather, not meat.

morphologies.name: Chitinous
morphologies.sensorReading: Dense keratin returns off every surface. Their hull plating and their bodies read as the same material.

morphologies.name: Energy-Being
morphologies.sensorReading: The lifesigns ARE the power grid. Your instruments cannot tell the crew from the reactor, and neither can you.

morphologies.name: Uplifted Fauna
morphologies.sensorReading: Familiar mammalian biology wearing unfamiliar cybernetics. Something raised these creatures up — recently, and in a hurry.

morphologies.name: Silicate
morphologies.sensorReading: Slow, mineral lifesigns — pulses minutes apart. They think in geological time and their ships are grown, not built.
